answer.answer:
Standardising a highly standardised design opens six distinct downstream capabilities, and they are not equal: reducing construction complexity, design for manufacture and assembly, kit-of-parts configurators, modular architecture and robotic assembly all rest on roughly a dozen or more of the fifty coded cases each, while the claim that standardisation lets you accommodate late design changes is carried by only two and is explicitly softened in its own source. Standardisation is also the thing industrialised-scale construction requires, so it sits upstream of industrialisation rather than following from it, and modular architecture feeds back into it in turn. Everything standardisation unlocks is a design attribute, an artefact, a process or a value: none of it is a machine, so the payoff is in how work is organised and specified, not in new equipment. No deployed project record bears on this question in the material in front of me, and the terms "product range" and "becomes possible" are not in the record, so the answer is framed in the record's own terms of standardisation and its outbound dependencies.

**What follows from AT7 "Highly standardised" (Attribute)**

AT7 carries exactly 6 outbound and 2 inbound dependency edges, and all of them are listed in the context, so the following set may be read as complete.

Outbound, in order of how many of the 50 coded cases carry the edge:

- AT7 enablesCapability VA7 "Reduce construction complexity", carried by 15 of the 50 coded cases [1], on the basis that the base module standard reduces component variety and coordinates design, manufacture and assembly, backed by standards evidence [2].
- AT7 enablesCapability PR9 "DfMA for DFAB process", carried by 13 of the 50 coded cases [1], with design standardisation and simplification as a DfMA enabler for offsite construction, peer-reviewed [1].
- AT7 enablesCapability AR6 "Configurators/kit-of-parts", on the basis that modular coordination permits the interchangeability of different components, backed by standards evidence [3]; the edge is carried by 11 of the 50 coded cases [1].
- AT7 enablesCapability AT2 "Modular", carried by 11 of the 50 coded cases [1], because decoupled standardised interfaces enable modular architecture and component interchange, peer-reviewed [4].
- AT7 enablesCapability PR4 "Robotic assembly", carried by 10 of the 50 coded cases, on the finding that Japanese automated erection systems rely on standardised prefabricated components, peer-reviewed [1].
- AT7 enablesCapability VA21 "Accommodate late design changes", carried by 2 of the 50 coded cases [1], and the supporting claim is a terminological review, softened in the record itself [5]. This is the weakest of the six by an order of magnitude against the strongest and should be treated as an open question rather than a design assumption.

Inbound, which is to say what standardisation is a requirement for or is produced by:

- AT8 "Industrialised" dependsOn AT7, since industrialised-construction scale depends on standardisation [6]; this edge is carried by 16 of the 50 coded cases [1], the largest count on any AT7 edge. Standardisation is upstream of industrialisation here, not a consequence of it.
- AT2 "Modular" enablesCapability AT7, because modular architecture reduces the variety of component sizes produced [7], carried by 11 of the 50 coded cases [1]. AT7 and AT2 therefore reinforce each other in both directions rather than one strictly preceding the other.

**Reach and category**

25 of the 50 coded cases draw on AT7 [1], so half the record is available to these edges; the per-edge counts above show how much of that half actually carries each pathway. AT7 is an Attribute [8], and its six targets are an Artefact (AR6), an Attribute (AT2), two Processes (PR9, PR4) and two Values (VA7, VA21). None is a Resource, so no machine sits directly downstream of standardisation in this set.

Onward reach worth noting: AR6 "Configurators/kit-of-parts" enablesCapability PR11 "Mass-customisation", carried by 9 of the 50 coded cases, where the design configurator integrates customisation data into robotic manufacturing, peer-reviewed [1], and PR9 "DfMA for DFAB process" enablesCapability PR5 "Modularisation", carried by 8 of the 50 coded cases [1]. So standardisation reaches mass-customisation at two removes rather than directly.

**Limits**

AT7 applies in the Design phase with a phase span of All [9], so these are design-stage commitments with downstream effect. The context carries no deployed process record, no census record and no firm against this question, so nothing here rests on a deployed case: the counts above tell you how many coded cases carry each edge, but the cases themselves are not in front of me. Note also that the countervailing risk RI15 "Design compromise/over standardised" is drawn on by 17 of the 50 coded cases [1], though it carries no dependency edges [1], so its relation to AT7 is not asserted in the record, only its prevalence.
